original.title: Exact multilevel Pell rigidity on every finite frontier
assumptions: The silver/Pell denominators and the exact three-child window recursion.
Selected maximizing root and its orientation; descendant gaps are nonnegative.

exactAuditedStatement: For an exact three-child Pell window recursion with finite globally attained maxima b_j, fixed orientationσ, and a maximizing root at n, the sum of oriented leaf gaps in a complete decomposition to scales k, k-1 equals Lambda_(n, k)=sum_{ell=k}^{n-1}q_(n-ell-1)S_ell. The stated finite frontier/ray corollaries hold with their positive-capacity guards.
hypotheses: b_j=max_s|W_j(s)|; for integer word discrepancies suprema are attained because range at fixed length finite.
Ray theorem requires b_(k-1),..., b_n>0and D=sum_{ell=k}^{n-1}S_ell/b_ell<1.
independentDerivationAndChecks: Define Gσ(m, s)=b_m-σW_m(s)>=0. Sum of child capacities is b_m+S_(m-1), while defects sum W_m; hence G(parent)+S=sum G(children). Each frontier expansion adds exactly its S, proving the general finite frontier identity by induction.

Complete silver-tree internal-node counts are q_(n-ell-1) at slack scale ell; check base n=k+1:(2leaves k,1leaf k-1,1internal). The 2,1 recursion propagates these and the leaf counts q_(n-k), q_(n-k-1). A maximizing aligned root has G0, proving the formula.

Every descendant subtree leaf set is a subset of the fixed root leaf set; nonnegativity gives G(v)+Lambda_(m, k)<=Lambda_(n, k). This is scoped to that tree. G=shortfall+2opposite-sign mass yields both unsigned identities; absolute-value telescope cancels internal defects.

Pell product bounds q_a q_c<=q_(a+c+1), proved by induction in the positive 2,1 recursion, yield Lambda<=D*C_(n, k), where the zero-slack capacity C=q_(n-k)b_k+q_(n-k-1)b_(k-1). Thus b_n=C-Lambda>=(1-D)C.

Normalized child gaps capacity-average to(g_parent+alpha)/(1+alpha), alpha=S_(m-1)/b_m. Choose a child with minimum ratio. Its1-g is at least(1-g_parent)/(1+alpha). D<1givesb_(ell+1)>b_ell and alpha_ell<=S_ell/b_ell. Products or1-product<=sum give every selected gap<=D and positive aligned defect.

For integer b, S with summable capped slack, eventually delta<1. Either b stays0, or once positive it stays positive and increases, and tail relative-slack sums tend0; this yields arbitrarily long finite near-rigid rays. No infinite ray in the original word follows: starts may drift. Counterframe/scalar stress claims are not premises for the identity or finite-ray theorem.
